intent: Read what happened at a provider in one account after the point the plugin's own cursor names: a thread that moved, a reply the provider detected, an invitation accepted, a message that bounced. Identifiers, moments and the provider's own flags travel; nothing anybody wrote does.

cursor.description: Where to read from: a cursor this plugin returned with an earlier page, handed back exactly as it was returned. Null when the read starts from a moment instead.

since.description: Read by date instead: every event at or after this moment. Null when the read starts from a cursor.

until.description: With since only: every event before this moment. Null reads up to now.

limit.description: At most this many events on the page. A page may come back shorter.

events.description: The events of this page, in the provider's own order.

cursor.description: Where the next read starts: passed back, it yields the events after this page. The plugin's own string, which nothing else reads.

has_more.description: Whether the provider holds more events after this page, to be read now with the cursor.

identifier.description: The provider's own identifier: printable ASCII with no space.

maybe_identifier.description: The provider's own identifier, or null where the event names none.

moment.description: When it happened, as the provider stamps it: in UTC, written with Z and no offset, to the second or to a fraction of it of at most seven digits.

thread_moved.description: A conversation thread of the account moved.

moved_by.description: Who moved it, in the provider's own word: other_side, a message the other side wrote; account, a message sent as the account; provider, a change with no message, such as a category or the read flag; null where the provider cannot say.

unread.description: Whether the provider holds the thread as unread.

has_meeting_intent.description: The provider's own judgement that the thread asks for a meeting, or null when it makes none.

reply_detected.description: The provider decided that a person replied.

invitation_accepted.description: A person accepted a connection invitation the account sent.

bounce.description: A message the account sent to a person bounced.
The provider's own word for the bounce, or null when it gives none.

failure_codes.when: the provider did not answer, or answered that it cannot be read for now
the provider refused the account's credential, or the account may not read its events
the account has no feed of events to read
the cursor handed back is one the provider no longer knows, or one this plugin can no longer read

conformance: Returns identifiers, moments and the provider's own flags, and nothing else: never a subject, a preview, a message's text or a name.
Returns a cursor with every page. Handed back, it yields the events after that page; it is the plugin's own string, and nothing else reads it.

Read by date, returns across the pages its cursors chain every event at or after since and, where until is given, before until. A provider that pages only by offset is paged newest first until the last item's moment passes since; a provider that holds less history answers what it holds and does not fail.
Reports a thread moved by other_side only for a message the other side wrote; a move by the account or by the provider is never reported as other_side.

Names a thread that moved by the identifier conversation.list returns as the thread's external_id, with occurred_at the moment the thread last moved — the moment conversation.list reports as its last_activity_at, to the millisecond — so that a move both reads find is said once.

Names, under campaign, the provider campaign a moved thread belongs to wherever the provider keeps one, by the identifier campaign.get pins, so that the runtime can leave that campaign's inbound read to the events; null is for a thread outside every provider campaign, a move that reaches, by the person, every campaign that is not archived and holds them as a member. Naming the campaign is still the right course, because the first rule decides alone when it finds one.

Reports moved_by null only where the provider cannot say who moved a thread. Such a move wakes the campaign's manager as a reply would, so a follow-up sent into a thread that already has a reply reads as one too.
Answers events_cursor_unknown for a cursor it can no longer read, so that the runtime reads again by date.
Answers events_unreachable for a provider that did not answer or is unavailable for now, so that the runtime reads again later.
Pins nothing: an answer that carries identifiers beside its result is refused.
Keeps its credential out of the binding, out of what it logs and out of what it returns: it reads it with host.env.
